motive: Mickey kept a ledger of every police payoff on the block, $200 a week to Sgt. O'Rourke among them, and planned to hand it to the Tribune. O'Rourke would have lost his badge, his pension, and his freedom.
opportunity: O'Rourke skipped his 1:30 callbox check, came down the alley and in through the unbolted cellar door, and was in the vault with Mickey at 1:30.
method: A blow to the head in the cellar vault; O'Rourke took the ledger.
verdictNarration: It was Sergeant Patrick O'Rourke. For years Mickey paid him two hundred a week to look the other way, and Mickey wrote every dollar down. When Mickey decided to take that ledger to the Tribune, O'Rourke decided Mickey's luck was finished. At half past one he skipped his callbox, came down the back alley in his uniform coat, and met Mickey in the vault. He walked out with the ledger. He left a button behind, and Ace Delaney, hiding his own crooked gin in the rain, saw the coat go down the stairs.

timeline.event: The Velvet Room closes; Vivian locks the front door.
Vivian and Mickey argue at the bar about selling the club; Frankie hears.
Ace slips into the alley to move his stolen gin crates.
O'Rourke skips his callbox check, enters by the alley cellar door, and strikes Mickey in the vault.
O'Rourke leaves by the alley with the ledger.

clues.name: Carbon copy page
clues.text: A carbon copy tucked behind the vault's hinge, missed by whoever took the ledger: "Sgt. P. O'R. — $200 weekly — paid."

clues.name: Brass button
clues.text: A brass button by the body, stamped with the Chicago Police star.

clues.name: Note on the till
clues.text: A note under the till in Mickey's scrawl: "Viv, we sell over my dead body. M."

clues.name: Train ticket
clues.text: Tucked in the dressing-room mirror: a one-way ticket to New York on the 6 am train, in Dolly's name.

clues.name: Callbox log
clues.text: The precinct callbox log at the alley mouth: Sgt. O'Rourke rang in at 1:00 and 2:00. The 1:30 check-in is blank.

clues.name: Gin crates
clues.text: Behind the garbage cans: six crates of top-shelf gin from Mickey's stock, chalk-marked "A.D."

orourke.personality: Jovial and back-slapping, treats the detective like an amateur, gets defensive about the badge.
orourke.deflection: Now listen, pal, I've been a cop since you were in short pants. Ask me something useful.

facts.text: Mickey and me go back a long ways. I kept this block quiet, and he kept the coffee hot.

facts.truth: I skipped my 1:30 callbox, came down the alley, and was in the cellar vault with Mickey at 1:30.
facts.lie_text: I was walking my Clark Street beat from one till I heard Frankie's whistle. Regular as a clock.
facts.lie_text_v2: I was out front on the sidewalk the whole time, keepin' an eye on the door. Never set foot inside.

facts.unlocked_text: So Mickey slipped me a little for looking the other way. Half the precinct's on somebody's list. That don't make me a killer.
Buttons fall off, detective. I was down there for a drink on Tuesday. Proves nothing.

facts.text: Ask the sister. Vivian wanted to sell this joint and Mickey wouldn't budge.
That piano man's always sneakin' crates out the back. Somebody oughta look into him.

dolly.personality: Theatrical and flirtatious, hides fear behind glamour, changes the subject with compliments.
dolly.innocentSecretReveal: Dolly Mae was skipping town. A New York club offered her top billing, and Mickey would never have let her go. She was packing in her dressing room when he died. She meant to leave him, not kill him.
dolly.deflection: Oh sugar, a lady never tells. Ask me something sweeter.

facts.text: Mickey gave me my first stage. He thought that meant he owned me.
I was in my dressing room behind the stage, taking off my face, from one till Frankie started screaming.

facts.unlocked_text: All right, I was skipping town. New York offered me the moon, and Mickey would never let me out. I'd have left him, sugar, not killed him.

facts.text: Just before half past one I heard the alley door bang and heavy boots on the cellar stairs. Not Frankie's shuffle.
Ace has been jumpy for weeks. I'd bet my last nickel he owes somebody.

frankie.personality: Fast-talking wisecracker, nervous, jokes when scared, eager to seem helpful.
frankie.innocentSecretReveal: Frankie Malone had been watering down Mickey's whiskey and pocketing the difference for a year. That's why he was so nervous. He was behind the bar washing glasses when Mickey died.
frankie.deflection: Ha! Look, pal, I just pour the drinks. You want answers, try a fortune teller.

facts.text: Eight years I've poured for Mickey. Best boss on the North Side, mostly.
I was behind the bar washing glasses from one until I went down to the cellar at a quarter to two.
Around ten past one Viv and Mickey went at it right here at the bar. Something about selling the place.
When I found him, the vault door was open and the alley door at the bottom of the stairs was unbolted. That door's always bolted.

ace.personality: Cool and unbothered on the surface, speaks in jazz slang, gets edgy when cornered.
ace.innocentSecretReveal: Ace Delaney was stealing Mickey's gin and selling it on the side. He was in the alley at half past one moving the crates, and he saw a man in a police coat go down the cellar stairs. He kept quiet to protect his hustle.
ace.deflection: Man, that's a tune I don't play. Ask me about the music.

facts.text: I play the keys, Mickey signs the checks. That's the whole song, daddy-o.

facts.truth: I was in the back alley moving stolen gin crates at 1:30.
facts.lie_text: I was at the piano, practicing a new number, till Frankie hollered.
facts.lie_text_v2: I was at the piano mostly. Maybe stepped out back for a smoke, a minute, tops.

facts.unlocked_text: Okay, the gin's mine. I was in the alley at half past one moving crates, and I saw a man in a police coat go down the cellar stairs. O'Rourke. Ain't nobody else on this block wears that coat.

facts.text: The alley door was banging around half past one. I figured it was the wind.
Viv wanted out of this joint bad. Money makes sisters mean.

vivian.personality: Sharp, controlled, contemptuous of fools, grief buried under business.
vivian.innocentSecretReveal: Vivian Doyle had a buyer from the Outfit and fought with Mickey about selling the Velvet Room. She was locking the front door at half past one. She wanted the money from the sale, not her brother's life.
vivian.deflection: I run a business, detective. I don't have time for questions like that.

facts.text: Mickey's my kid brother. We built this place together from one bathtub of gin.
At half past one I was at the front door counting the night's take. Nobody out front but the rain. Not a soul, not even the cop.

facts.unlocked_text: Yes, we fought. I had a buyer and Mickey said no. You don't kill your brother over a sale, detective.

facts.text: Frankie found him. I heard him yelling at a quarter to two and ran down.
Mickey was scared this week. He said someone with a badge was squeezing him.
